title: Context Compression for DeepSeek Sparse Attention Architectures
text:
An LLM agent accumulates history as it reads code, calls tools, runs experiments, and processes their results. A short initial request can become a long sequence of constraints, plans, file contents, errors, repairs, and intermediate findings. Eventually, the agent must make room for new information to continue working within its available context capacity.
This is the setting for auto compact: automatically reducing the memory occupied by existing context while preserving the state needed for subsequent work. Losing a constraint can change the agent’s future behavior. Losing a tool result can cause it to repeat an operation it has already completed.
This post examines reference queries, cache selection, and value merging for DSA and MLA, followed by a recovery stage that uses an arriving question to restore local details. Most results use DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731; the V3.2 implementation helps explain some DSA-specific adaptations.
One current observation is that query-independent A60 scores 244/473 on the retained LongBench-v2 cohort, while query-guided recovery scores 258/473, at a mean final document retention of 63.42%. The recovery configuration uses additional capacity and computation, and its head selection has development-set overlap. These conditions are discussed alongside the results.

title: Context Compression for DeepSeek Sparse Attention Architectures
section: 1 What Auto Compact Should Remember
text:
1 What Auto Compact Should Remember

1.1 A running task has several kinds of state
An agent’s history contains user requirements, actions already taken, externally observed facts, and unresolved questions. Their future importance differs. Hundreds of installation-log lines may admit substantial reduction, while an instruction such as “do not upload to GitHub yet” must continue to govern subsequent actions.
Given a processed history H, we want a smaller memory M(H) that preserves useful behavior after subsequent input U arrives:

p_\theta(y\mid M(H),U)\approx p_\theta(y\mid H,U).

Here, U can be a new user instruction, a tool response, or another stage of the task. A reusable memory must support inputs that are not fully known when compaction occurs.


1.2 Text summaries and cache memory
One approach summarizes the history into text and uses that text as new context. Such memory is readable, inspectable, and easy to save between sessions. Another approach retains a compact KV cache that subsequent tokens can access directly.
This project explores cache memory. Method A keeps selected original cache rows; E1 also merges value information. The resulting state depends on the model, quantization format, and inference backend, so transferring it between models requires additional compatibility work.
Fast KV Compaction via Attention Matching develops a framework for constructing compact caches through attention matching. This implementation draws on that framework and adapts selected ideas to sparse routing and MLA’s shared latent representation. A and E1 below refer to the particular definitions used here.


1.3 Known questions and unknown future inputs
When the downstream question is already available, a compressor can prioritize information relevant to that question. Auto compact also needs to operate before the next instruction has arrived.
We therefore distinguish task-aware reference construction, which includes the real question, from generic document study, which uses the document and a general study instruction. The latter approximates reusable memory construction. Once a real question arrives, a recovery stage can supplement that memory with local details.

title: Context Compression for DeepSeek Sparse Attention Architectures
section: 2 Why Compact a Sparse Attention Cache
text:
2 Why Compact a Sparse Attention Cache

2.1 Sparse access and total storage
DSA uses an indexer to select candidates for the current query, followed by main attention over those candidates. The DeepSeek-V3.2 model description identifies sparse attention as a component of its long-context efficiency.
Sparse access limits how many positions participate in each main-attention step. Historical cache rows still provide the candidates for future steps. Compaction reduces the physical cache that remains available and keeps the main-attention and indexer layouts consistent.
The distinction matters for memory quality. Once a row has been removed, it cannot directly participate in a later query’s attention. Recovering it requires retaining a source elsewhere.


2.2 Shared MLA latents constrain value merging
MLA uses a compact latent representation. Information used for key scoring and value reading is not stored as two completely independent tensors that can be rewritten arbitrarily.
Overwriting a shared latent with a merged value can therefore change key scores as well. E1 preserves the original key-dependent representation and stores the value update in separate delta pages. The attention correction uses the same probabilities derived from the retained keys.


2.3 V4 has heterogeneous native rows
The local V4 implementation includes C4 layers with one long-term cache row per four raw tokens and C128 layers with one row per 128 raw tokens. The scheduler tracks lengths in raw-token units.
A rewrite must expose a common scheduler-visible length while retaining different exact row counts for different layer types. The current plan uses 256-token alignment and preserves boundary rows that do not lie completely inside the document. A target such as 60% document retention consequently differs slightly from the realized retention.

title: Context Compression for DeepSeek Sparse Attention Architectures
section: 3 Constructing Reference Queries
text:
3 Constructing Reference Queries

3.1 Collecting Q through an additional forward pass
The importance of a cached position depends on the queries that will access it. A detail ignored during ordinary narration may become essential when a later question asks for a precise date or a local code behavior.
A reference pass processes a suffix after the document and collects the resulting Q vectors at each layer. These vectors measure routing frequency and attention contribution over the original cache, producing scores for selection.
The generic suffix contains a document-study instruction, a chat-template tail, and tokens sampled at evenly spaced positions across the document. The instruction asks the model to attend to central claims, entities, relationships, numbers, exceptions, and easily missed details.
The document portion is assembled directly from existing token IDs. It does not require autoregressively generating a summary; it provides a controlled set of forward-pass probes.


3.2 Relating the Q budget to retained rows
Let B be the document budget-block size and \rho the target retention. A block retains approximately t=\operatorname{round}(\rho B) positions, with reference budget

n=\left\lceil\lambda t\right\rceil,\qquad\lambda=2.5.

For A60, B=1024, t=614, and n=1535. The default suffix contains a 93-token study instruction, a two-token template tail, and 1535 sampled document tokens: 1630 tokens in total. The scorer selects 1535 reference Q positions evenly across that suffix1.


Note 1
Suffix length and scoring-Q count are distinct. The default 1630-token suffix supplies 1535 scored Q positions. Fixed-length 512, 1024, and 2048 suffix experiments score every reference position. The 1024-token document block distributes retention quotas across the entire document.


3.3 Coverage remains approximate
A generic reference approximates future access patterns. A low-scoring passage may still matter for an unfamiliar question, particularly when it contains a rare entity, code detail, or implicit condition.
This motivates combining broad memory construction with selective recovery after a concrete question becomes available.

title: Context Compression for DeepSeek Sparse Attention Architectures
section: 4 Cache Selection and Value Merging
text:
4 Cache Selection and Value Merging

4.1 A selects representatives within each block
The V3.2 implementation combines root-mean-square main-attention importance with the square root of indexer selection frequency, normalizing each component before adding them. The V4 C4 path combines accumulated main-attention mass and routing counts after separate normalization. Its C128 path uses main-attention mass.
For a V4 C4 row j, let m_j be its accumulated reference attention mass and r_j its routing count. The proxy score used for base selection is

s_j=\frac{m_j}{\sum_km_k+\epsilon}
    +\frac{r_j}{\sum_kr_k+\epsilon}.

Each document block corresponding to 1024 raw tokens receives a proportional retention quota. High-scoring rows are selected within that block, ensuring coverage across document positions rather than allowing a few regions to consume the entire budget.
Let S_\ell denote a layer’s selected set. A preserves its original rows and moves them into a compact physical layout in their original order. Different layers can select different contents while satisfying the required common length.


4.2 E1 merges values while retaining key scoring
E1 uses the same selected positions. Each source position is assigned to the nearest retained representative by position within its block, and the representative receives an attention-mass-weighted value average.
For cluster C_j, original values v_i, and reference masses m_i,

\bar v_j=\frac{\sum_{i\in C_j}m_i v_i}
                    {\sum_{i\in C_j}m_i+\epsilon},\qquad
\Delta v_j=\bar v_j-v_j.

A cluster with negligible mass falls back to the original representative. The key-dependent cache remains unchanged, while separate pages store \Delta v_j. With probabilities \alpha_j(q) derived from retained keys, the correction is

o_{\mathrm{E1}}(q)=o_{\mathrm{A}}(q)+\sum_{j\in S}\alpha_j(q)\Delta v_j.

V3.2 performs this operation in latent value space; V4 uses its native cache-value representation and quantized write path. This implements the specified merged-value computation. Approximation to full-context attention still depends on selection, merging error, and the queries encountered later.


4.3 Retained-row ratio is only one cost measure
E1 requires delta pages and attention correction. A60 and E1-60 consequently share a base candidate-row budget, while their total cache bytes differ.
For an agent, the relevant comparison includes task quality, remaining capacity for new tokens, total held blocks, and additional latency. These costs determine whether value merging is useful in practice.

title: Context Compression for DeepSeek Sparse Attention Architectures
section: 5 Making the Cache Rewrite Usable
text:
5 Making the Cache Rewrite Usable

5.1 Update both cache streams and the scheduler
Selected indices must become a state from which normal generation can continue. The implementation moves main and indexer rows consistently, rewrites scheduler and Model Runner block tables, and returns unneeded tail pages to the pool.
Rows are copied forward in bounded chunks. Original-order selection ensures that destinations do not overwrite unread source rows. E1 reserves its delta pages separately from the preallocated pool and keeps them disjoint from every live source-request page during rewriting.
Because vLLM preallocates its pool, returning blocks need not reduce the process’s GPU-memory reading. Request-held blocks, returned blocks, and remaining pool capacity measure the resulting headroom more directly.


5.2 Preserve original positional coordinates
Compaction changes physical addresses while retained rows still originate from different historical positions. The implementation maintains the mapping required for logical causality and RoPE.
A token originally at position 10,000 may move to physical position 6,000. Its original positional meaning and its new storage address must remain consistent with subsequent queries.
Freeing physical capacity and extending the model’s positional range are separate concerns. Original coordinates continue growing as more history arrives. The streaming experiment below explicitly prepares a larger position-lookup capacity; task quality at those positions still requires evaluation.


5.3 Rewind temporary reference and probe state
Reference and probe passes create temporary cache and sliding-window state. Those states are rewound before formal answering. The real query is then replayed on the final cache.
“One long-prefix prefill” thus includes additional short forwards: the reference pass and two passes over the short query. It avoids recomputing the entire long document while retaining the costs necessary for scoring and probing.

title: Context Compression for DeepSeek Sparse Attention Architectures
section: 6 Recovering Details After a Question Arrives
text:
6 Recovering Details After a Question Arrives

6.1 Freeze generic memory before probing
The recovery pipeline first computes query-independent scores s_\ell and selections S_\ell over C_{\mathrm{full}}, then freezes both. A real-query probe reads only the logical view corresponding to S_\ell. The single-compaction experiment temporarily keeps the full cache until one final physical rewrite.
Probe signals therefore come from the visible compressed memory. Excluded rows are not read to score themselves. Once recovery regions have been selected, missing content is restored from the retained full-cache source.






Figure 1: Generic selection, restricted query probing, and final materialization. The full cache remains available for restoration, while the probe can access only frozen S.





6.2 Read window signals from four MLA heads
The configuration uses global heads L20-H5, L20-H30, L20-H31, and L26-H58. Attention signals are aggregated into windows of 128 raw tokens.
For head h, query position q, and window w, sum native probabilities over visible rows in that window:

a_{h,q,w}=\sum_{j\in S_\ell\cap w}\alpha_{h,q,j}.

Normalization includes the actual routed C4 rows, causal sliding-window attention, and the attention sink. Reconstructed outputs are checked against the native kernel to avoid treating locally normalized proxy scores as the probabilities used by the model.
For each head and window, average the five largest values over the complete query, using all positions if fewer than five exist. Z-normalize each head across available windows, then average equally across heads:

u_{h,w}=\operatorname{MeanTop5}_{q}(a_{h,q,w}),\qquad
g_w=\frac{1}{4}\sum_h\operatorname{Z}_{w}(u_{h,w}).

The highest-scoring 24 windows define recovery region R, covering at most 24\times128=3072 raw tokens. A window without any surviving representative cannot be located directly using these retained-row signals.


6.3 Additive and fixed-budget restoration
Convert R into the native row set R_\ell for each layer. Additive recovery keeps the original selection and inserts missing rows:

S'_\ell=S_\ell\cup R_\ell.

A common scheduler length requires alignment across heterogeneous layers. Remaining slots are filled with high-scoring original rows, so the physical addition depends on actual missing rows and is not simply 3072 tokens.
Fixed-budget recovery inserts the missing rows and removes an equal number of low-scoring rows from S_\ell\setminus R_\ell, using the frozen original scores:

S'_\ell=(S_\ell\cup R_\ell)
\setminus\operatorname{BottomK}_{s_\ell}(S_\ell\setminus R_\ell).

This preserves base row counts, but the displaced rows may matter for later tasks. All recovery results reported below use the additive policy. Fixed-budget recovery remains implemented; numerical results for it are not reported here.


6.4 Recovery needs a surviving source
The single-compaction pipeline retains C_{\mathrm{full}} until materialization. Multi-round streaming instead archives actual native cache rows to CPU. The query locates a region; the retained source supplies content that has left the GPU.
A discarded row cannot reappear through a set-union operation without such a source. CPU cache, original tool records, and retrieval-based memory are possible directions for persistent agents, with their storage and access costs included in the system budget.

10 Multi-Round Streaming Beyond a Single Window

10.1 Read, compact, and append
The separate over-capacity cohort contains 30 questions with full documents of approximately 1.10 million to 4.64 million tokens, averaging 2.00 million.
Streaming reserves capacity for references, the question, generation, and safety margin. When the active physical prefix reaches its threshold, it applies query-independent A60, returns pages, and continues reading unseen source tokens. An under-capacity final tail is kept without an additional terminal A pass.
Recorded questions trigger one to nine compactions. Every source document token receives one document forward pass. Later tokens attend to the memory produced by earlier rounds, so the resulting cache also differs from a hypothetical full-document forward pass without intermediate compaction.


10.2 CPU archives support final restoration
Actual native rows are archived on CPU with their original coordinates. The real question arrives only after document reading finishes and probes the current physical GPU memory. The selected 24 windows are then restored from the archive.
This bounds active GPU-cache capacity while allowing the CPU archive to grow with history. It represents one form of hierarchical memory with a small active state and a larger recoverable past.

title: Context Compression for DeepSeek Sparse Attention Architectures
section: 11 Toward Sustained Agent Tasks
text:
11 Toward Sustained Agent Tasks

11.1 Trigger policies and protected capacity
A candidate integration triggers compaction near an active-cache threshold while reserving space for tool results, probes, and generation. User constraints, current plans, recent actions, and important tool conclusions may benefit from explicit protection. Existing experiments protect non-document instructions and suffixes; they do not implement those finer agent-state policies.
An available question can trigger recovery when the budget permits. Before such a question exists, the system maintains generic memory. Triggering and recovery size should account for available capacity and task requirements rather than always applying an identical restoration budget.


11.2 Forgetting can accumulate across rounds
Information lost in one round can remain absent from all subsequent references. A CPU archive preserves a source, but retained-row probe signals may still fail to identify the needed region.
Further work should study memory-age budgets, explicit protection of critical state, and retrieval from original text or tool history. Single-compaction QA accuracy alone cannot establish behavior after many compactions.


11.3 What to evaluate next
The next priority is evaluation on real multi-step tasks: whether constraints persist, completed operations are repeated, cross-file debugging loses dependencies, and task completion changes after successive compactions. Comparisons should include textual summarization, truncation, pure A, E1, and cache memory with external recovery under comparable actual capacity and computation budgets.
Heads and budgets should be selected on an independent discovery cohort and frozen before evaluation on new tasks. Current measurements justify further exploration of the approach. The longer-term objective is memory that lets agents continue reliable work under capacity constraints.

title: From a Model’s Random-Number Fingerprint:A Study of LLM Reasoning Circuits
text:
Discussions about GPT “getting worse” or being routed to a smaller model never really stop. A LINUX DO post proposed a simple test: repeatedly ask a model to choose a random number from a fixed range, estimate its output distribution, and use that distribution as a statistical fingerprint of the model1.
It is easy to see why this method works and why it is useful. But it also suggests a more interesting research question:
To investigate this question, we began with the prompt 「在 1–300 中随机选择一个数」(English translation: “Choose a random number from 1 to 300”) and located a class of heads that strongly read the candidate-range boundary 300 (Sec 2). Further experiments gradually revealed their more general role: reading the candidate set in a reasoning task. When the answer has not yet been successfully inferred and the model must still choose among candidates, the information these heads write into the residual stream markedly changes the output (Sec 3).
When we manually interrupt the model’s reasoning circuit during otherwise normal reasoning—for example, by deleting a key reasoning chain or blocking retrieval heads—and thereby force the model into uncertain reasoning, the causal effects of these heads are likewise amplified (Sec 4). This suggests that two circuits compete inside the model: when the model can reason normally, the reasoning circuit operates while the circuit corresponding to these heads is suppressed;when the reasoning circuit is interrupted, this other circuit gains causal influence and begins to dominate the model’s behavior.
Based on this, we use the behavior of these heads as a signal of whether the model’s reasoning is reliable and trigger a reasoning-enhancement strategy when unreliable reasoning is detected. The results show that it can indeed detect unreliable reasoning and improve model performance (Sec 5). Additional experiments show that these heads also exist in models with linear-attention and sparse-attention architectures (Sec 6).

title: From a Model’s Random-Number Fingerprint:A Study of LLM Reasoning Circuits
section: 1 Background: Non-random Outputs from LLMs
text:
1 Background: Non-random Outputs from LLMs
Suppose we give a language model the following prompt:

请从 1–300 随机选择一个数，只输出这个数字。

(English translation: “Choose a random number from 1 to 300. Output only the number.”)
The model does not literally draw a random number during its forward pass. More precisely, a language model’s forward pass is a deterministic function from the input text to the logits for the next token. The decoder then uses a temperature T to turn those logits into a probability distribution:

p_i = \frac{\exp(z_i/T)}{\sum_j \exp(z_j/T)}.

With both the prompt and decoding configuration fixed, the model’s next-token probability distribution p is fixed as well2.
Under sampling, a pseudorandom number generator selects a token from the distribution p. Individual outputs can vary, while the long-run statistical distribution should remain stable. This is why random-number choice can serve as a model fingerprint: different parameter sets assign different but stable probabilities to number tokens, and repeated sampling turns those preferences into a recognizable output distribution.


Note 2
Real inference services are not necessarily reproducible bit for bit. Batching and parallel reductions in backends such as vLLM and SGLang can change the order of floating-point operations and introduce numerical differences. See Thinking Machines Lab’s Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference.
The question we really care about is: How is this probability distribution written and generated during the model’s forward pass?

title: From a Model’s Random-Number Fingerprint:A Study of LLM Reasoning Circuits
section: 2 The Head That Writes the Random-Number Fingerprint
text:
2 The Head That Writes the Random-Number Fingerprint
During an LLM forward pass, QK determines where attention reads from, while OV determines what is written into the residual stream. That information is read and processed by MoE layers before the output layer produces a logit distribution.
Under this picture, a reasonable hypothesis is that some deep-layer heads encode the range 1–300, so downstream computation can read the candidate range. That information is written into the residual stream and shapes the output; the model’s selection preference is written along the way.
To test this hypothesis, we ran experiments on the MoE model Qwen3-235B-A22B. We constructed multiple Chinese prompts similar to 「请从1-300随机选择一个数，只输出这个数字」 (English translation: “Choose a random number from 1 to 300. Output only the number.”). All ask the model to select a random number from 1–300, but use different semantic phrasings.
The exact probabilities vary across prompts, but their overall structure remains stable: almost all next-token probability mass is assigned to digits, and 1 and 2 consistently form the dominant competition3.


Note 3
I suspect that the high probability of 1 and 2 relative to other digits reflects the numerical distribution in the pretraining corpus. The pronounced preference between 1 and 2, however, seems more likely to be encoded during post-training.




P(1)
P(2)
P(3\text{–}9)
P(\text{digit})




49.39%
49.74%
0.73%
99.86%




We therefore use “which head most strongly disrupts this generation preference?” as the criterion for locating the key head.

2.1 Head localization
Qwen3-235B-A22B has 94 layers and 64 query heads per layer. We examined each head through ablation: immediately before the layer’s attention o_proj, we zeroed the target head’s 128-dimensional output slice at every input-token position while leaving all other computation unchanged.
We measured the change between the original and ablated full-vocabulary distributions with total variation distance:


\operatorname{TV}(h,l)
=\operatorname{TV}\!\left(p,p^{(h,l)}\right)
=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{v\in\mathcal V}
\left|p(v)-p^{(h,l)}(v)\right|.


Here, p is the original next-token distribution, while p^{(h,l)} is the distribution after ablating head (h,l). A larger TV means that the head has a stronger causal effect on the current output distribution.
We identified L82.H18 as the most significant head. Its full-vocabulary TV reached 34.0%, the strongest effect among all heads4.


Note 4
L82.H18 also ranks first by centered full-vocabulary logit \operatorname{RMS}_{c}(h,l), defined as:

\operatorname{RMS}_{c}(h,l)=
\sqrt{\frac{1}{|\mathcal V|}\sum_{v\in\mathcal V}
\left(\Delta z_v^{(h,l)}-\overline{\Delta z}^{(h,l)}\right)^2}.

Here, \Delta z_v^{(h,l)} is the change in token v’s logit after ablating head (h,l), and \overline{\Delta z}^{(h,l)} is its full-vocabulary mean. \operatorname{RMS}_{c}(h,l) represents the overall effect of ablating that head on the full-vocabulary logit structure.





Figure 1(a): Local TV landscape around L82.H18.







Figure 1(b): Changes in P(1) and P(2) after ablating L82.H18.




After ablating L82.H18, P(1) decreased for every prompt, with a mean change of −33.80 percentage points; meanwhile, P(2) changed by an average of +33.54 percentage points, while the remaining output probabilities were nearly unchanged.
This shows that the identified L82.H18 does indeed write a strong preference within the set of numerical candidates.


2.2 Head attention distribution
We next examine the attention distribution of L82.H18. All prompts used here contain 28 tokens and share a similar structure: 300 is split across t7–t9, the model-side assistant token is at t22, and the final \n\n before the answer is at t27.




Figure 2: The 28-token random-number prompt after applying the chat template.



The most concentrated attention connection of L82.H18 runs from token \n\n at t27 to token 300 at t7–t9, with an average attention mass of 99.56%. The figure below shows the attention distributions for five representative prompts.




Figure 3: L82.H18@q27 attention across five representative prompts. Each row represents one prompt, each column a token position, and token 300 always occupies t7–t9.



In other words, as the model prepares its answer, L82.H18 reads almost exclusively from the range boundary 300 and writes the resulting vector at the start of the answer.


2.3 Head attention intervention
To determine whether the prominent attention edge actually dominates the output shift, we performed the following L82.H18 attention interventions on the same prompts:


Full model: no intervention; this is the baseline.
Remove L82.H18: zero the output of L82.H18 at every token position.
Remove the \n\n → 300 attention edges: zero only the three edges from q27 to t7–t9.
Remove L82.H18, then restore the \n\n → 300 write: first remove L82.H18, then add back at t27 the original residual-write vector contributed predominantly by t7–t9; the other token positions remain ablated.


The first three experiments test whether the \n\n → 300 attention edges dominate the behavior of L82.H18. The fourth restores the information these edges write into the residual stream, testing whether it recovers the effect of the complete head.




Figure 4: The probabilities of generating tokens 1 and 2, and full-vocabulary TV, under four conditions: full model, remove L82.H18, remove \n\n → 300 attention edges, and remove L82.H18 then restore the \n\n → 300 write.



The results show that removing the \n\n → 300 attention edges reaches 96.95% of the effect of removing the complete L82.H18 head. After removing L82.H18, restoring only the residual write dominated by these edges recovers 97.33% of the original deletion effect.
This suggests that the main role of L82.H18 is to transport candidate-range information to the answer position and thereby help form the model’s output fingerprint.

3 Head Generalization Experiments
So far, we have demonstrated the behavior of L82.H18 when choosing a random number from 1 to 300. The next question is how well this behavior generalizes: can L82.H18 aggregate and transport candidate information to help form a model fingerprint in other tasks, and can it serve a more general function?
To answer this question, we varied candidate types and constraints, downstream tasks, and reasoning length to examine the head’s function across settings.

3.1 Candidate-Type Generalization Experiments
We began with the most direct generalization: if numerical candidates are replaced by another type of candidate, does L82.H18 exhibit the same properties? We replaced the original 1–300 range with an alphabetic range:

请从 A 到 D 中任选一个，只输出这个字母。

(English translation: “Choose any letter from A to D and output only that letter.”)
The result closely mirrors the numerical-range experiment: L82.H18 assigns 88.62% attention to the letter D, and deleting this prominent attention edge produces 30.3% TV.
We then expanded the candidates into explicit lists to test whether this property extends to general candidate sets. Every experiment used the same template:

(English translation: “Choose any item from the candidate list 【…】 and output only the selected item.”)
We constructed a range of candidate lists, including canonical and non-canonical lists.

Canonical lists: the elements have a strong intrinsic order and are presented in that order, such as the heavenly-stem list 【甲, 乙, 丙, 丁, …】.
Non-canonical lists: the elements have no stable intrinsic order and are arranged without a canonical sequence, such as the food list 【dumplings, noodles, rice, buns, …】.

We keep the input range fixed at 1–300, construct a variety of downstream tasks, and observe the head’s behavior. Initial experiments suggest that the head’s effectiveness is related to the number of valid candidates allowed by the task. Specifically, we divide the tasks into two groups:

3.5 Generalizing Candidate-Information-Transport Heads
The preceding experiments use L82.H18 as their subject. As noted in Sec 3.1, however, this group of heads has a strong causal effect only when a list has a pronounced internal order.
Do lists with weaker order relations also have a family of heads with a similar function? From the perspective of Transformer circuits, such heads should exist8. We therefore test whether comparable heads can be found on general lists.

title: From a Model’s Random-Number Fingerprint:A Study of LLM Reasoning Circuits
section: 4 Causal Effects of Heads Under Reasoning-Circuit Interruption
text:
4 Causal Effects of Heads Under Reasoning-Circuit Interruption
The experiments in Sec 3 identified a family of heads with the following function:

When the answer has not yet been successfully inferred and the model must still choose among multiple candidates,downstream computation relies strongly on the candidate information transported by these heads.

This behavior generalizes across candidate lists, constraints on the candidate set, task types, and answers that involve long-form thinking.
We can also view this result through the lens of Transformer circuits. A model’s forward pass is not determined by one signal: multiple circuits write different signals into the residual stream, and those signals jointly shape the output. One useful way to understand their interaction is:

Ordinarily, the strongest signal dominates the model’s behavior. Other signals remain present but are suppressed in the competition. If the dominant circuit weakens or is interrupted, a weaker circuit may gain relative weight and compensate for the missing information. This competition may be especially apparent in larger models whose information representations are more distributed.

From this perspective, the heads we found jointly participate in a circuit: when the model can reason normally, the deterministic reasoning signal dominates, the writes of this circuit have little effect on the final output, and removing them produces little TV;when the normal reasoning signal weakens or its circuit is interrupted, this circuit gains greater causal influence and removing it produces substantially larger TV.
The experiments in Sec 3.3 and Sec 3.4 already provide initial support for this account. We now test it with active interventions, using multiple methods to damage the model’s normal reasoning circuit and observing whether the causal effect of the candidate heads grows as expected.

4.1 Interrupting the Start of the Circuit: Removing Input Evidence
One direct way to disrupt normal reasoning is to remove the decisive evidence from the input, thereby damaging the start of the reasoning pathway.
We construct counterfactual question-answer cases from DROP, BrowseComp-Plus, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and MuSiQue. Each question is rewritten so that the correct answer and other candidates are replaced by randomly generated temporary codes. Neither the spelling nor the numbers in the codes reveal a pattern, preventing the model from answering through parametric memory.
Each case has a complete-evidence version and a missing-evidence version:

Complete evidence: retain all evidence in the input so the model can reason normally.
Missing evidence: remove the key evidence required for reasoning so the model cannot infer the correct answer.

At the start of the answer, we jointly ablate the writes of the heads selected in Sec 3.5 and measure the full-vocabulary TV.

4.2 Interrupting the Middle of the Circuit: Removing the Key Reasoning Chain
Next, we remove the key chain in the model’s thinking that makes it possible to infer the answer, then observe how the heads’ causal effects change. This can be viewed as disrupting the middle of the reasoning circuit.
We use the counterfactual datasets from Sec 4.1 and the heads localized in Sec 3.5, constructing a complete-reasoning-chain version and a missing-reasoning-chain version:

4.3 Interrupting the End of the Circuit: Removing Retrieval Heads
The preceding interventions interrupt the beginning and middle of the reasoning circuit. We now consider its end: keep the question and input evidence intact, but block the retrieval heads responsible for transporting the answer from context9. Although the answer evidence remains, the model loses the ability to use it.


Note 9
For the definition and role of retrieval heads, see Retrieval Head Mechanistically Explains Long-Context Factuality. Some of my recent experiments suggest that, at the end of a reasoning circuit, retrieval heads transport an answer already identified by the model from context to the decoding position.

section: 5 Improving Reasoning by Detecting Head TV
text:
5 Improving Reasoning by Detecting Head TV
The preceding experiments clarify the function of the candidate-information heads: when the answer has not been effectively inferred, their effect on the output distribution grows substantially. Can we use this mechanism to improve the model’s reasoning performance? Specifically, can we enhance performance as follows?

After normal reasoning produces an answer, measure the candidate heads’ TV,and, if TV exceeds a threshold, spend additional resources to strengthen reasoning.

We again test on DROP, BrowseComp-Plus, 2WikiMultiHopQA, and MuSiQue, constructing an agent-style workflow in which the model reasons from retrieved information. After reasoning ends and the answer is produced, we ablate the heads’ writes at the position where the final response begins and measure the full-vocabulary TV10.


Note 10
Because intervention is required only at the final \n\n position before the formal answer, all preceding tokens can reuse the prefix cache, keeping TV detection inexpensive. In our implementation, vLLM’s llm.collective_rpc() calls set_rag_tv_probe() on each worker to switch candidate-head ablation on and off.
Based on the results in Sec 4, we empirically fix the TV threshold at 6%. When TV exceeds this threshold, the agent continues the workflow, supplies the model with more retrieved information, and appends a new user prompt stating that the previous output may lack evidence and asking the model to continue reasoning and determine the answer.




Figure 9: Head-TV-gated reasoning enhancement on each dataset, showing the baseline reasoning success rate, frequency of TV exceeding the threshold, and success rate after reasoning enhancement.



Across all four datasets, TV detection identifies trajectories that have not been reasoned through effectively, and reasoning enhancement improves success rates. TV detection can therefore serve as a proxy for unreliable reasoning and provide a degree of repair.
An important qualification is that the method can detect only unreliable reasoning in which the model has not formed a stable internal reasoning circuit;reasoning that the model considers reliable but that is in fact wrong cannot be detected through TV.

These two real trajectories illustrate this boundary. In trajectory A, the model’s reasoning already contains signs of guessing, and TV exceeds the threshold, so it is detected and successfully triggers enhanced reasoning. In trajectory B, the model forms a complete and definite reasoning chain; although the answer is wrong, TV does not reach the threshold and the error is missed11.

Even so, experiments show that reasoning trajectories like B still have substantially higher TV than reliable and correct trajectories. This suggests that some unreliable or uncertain signals, although absent from the model’s natural-language output, still alter the representation space and can therefore be detected through TV.
Candidate-information-head TV can therefore be viewed as a proxy for unreliable reasoning. Of course, unreliable signals may also appear in the model’s reasoning chain, but TV can additionally detect signals that are not expressed in natural language (as described in Note 11). Other measures, such as the distribution entropy of generated tokens, can also capture related signals, but these token-level metrics are local proxies and cannot identify uncertainty across the full reasoning process as TV can.

title: From a Model’s Random-Number Fingerprint:A Study of LLM Reasoning Circuits
section: 7 Summary and Reflections
text:
7 Summary and Reflections
Starting from the model fingerprint that appears consistently in random-number selection tasks, this post identifies a class of heads that transport candidate information. We find that when the answer has not been effectively inferred and the model must still choose among multiple candidates, these heads exert a substantial causal effect. Their role generalizes across candidates, tasks, and architectures, and is reproduced consistently in multiple intervention experiments that interrupt the normal reasoning circuit. We further use the TV of these heads as a detection signal for unreliable reasoning and use it to trigger additional reasoning enhancement, thereby improving the model’s reasoning performance.
Of course, this post does not fully explain how the model’s fingerprint is formed. I initially hoped to analyze how the random-number fingerprint emerges, but I subsequently realized that this question is difficult to study without examining the training data or training dynamics. Moreover, only a small number of trajectories during post-training can substantially alter a model’s preferences, making the analysis even harder. After realizing this, I changed direction, began observing the model’s information flow, and gradually arrived at the results presented in this post.
Among all the experimental phenomena, the most thought-provoking is the competition between information circuits in the model: why does the TV produced by ablating candidate-information heads increase after the reasoning circuit is interrupted? One direct view is that the signal strength of these heads remains unchanged, but interrupting the reasoning circuit increases the model’s perplexity and makes the logits and probability distribution more uniform, so the impact of a fixed-strength signal grows accordingly.
This view is not necessarily wrong, but an account based only on logits or softmax is too post hoc to explain many observations. Logits themselves do not change in a consistent direction, nor do the heads affect logits consistently. In the experiments in Sec 5, there are also several cases in which the model’s output distribution is extremely sharp during unreliable reasoning, yet TV remains substantial. Nor can we explain why only the localized heads have a large effect on the output distribution when their absolute effect on the logits is small and sometimes even slight. Judging from the ablation results, the heads writing more information, the network propagating the same write more strongly, and the final softmax becoming more sensitive seem to occur simultaneously and remain coupled.
Even so, the current findings are already sufficient to improve reasoning performance. This is also the point of understanding models, or of interpretability work: it should solve concrete problems or be useful enough, rather than explain merely for explanation’s sake, and it must especially consider different levels of generalization. Work such as J-Space similarly begins with an understanding of the model and ultimately proposes a method that constrains model behavior. How to understand the model better within the current framework remains a question for future study.

title: DeepSeek 稀疏注意力架构下的上下文压缩
text:
在使用像 Codex 这样的 LLM Agent 时，我们应该都遇到过这样的场景：随着工作流的进行，Agent 上下文长度不断增长，当长度逼近 LLM 窗口上限或者提前设定的阈值时，插件就会触发上下文自动压缩，为后续工作流腾出上下文空间。
这就是所谓的 Auto-compaction 技术，其目的是在压缩 LLM 上下文占用的同时，完整保留 Agent 后续工作流所需的关键状态。根据公开资料，目前各家的 Agent 工具大多是通过生成文本摘要来执行这一过程的，例如 Kimi Code、Claude Code 以及 Gemini CLI。不过，我体感上下文压缩做得最好的 Codex，其具体压缩算法我们仍不得而知，其技术文档中明确提到，它使用了远端原生压缩（remote native compaction），并且明确指出并非生成式摘要。
事实上，通过 Prompt 让模型做生成式摘要，是一种偏上层的工程折中；相比之下，远端原生压缩则更接近模型的本质。从这一角度思考，一个自然的切入点便是从 KV Cache 层面，实现原生的上下文压缩，而这又与模型的架构和注意力实现方式息息相关。
在目前的开源生态下，最新一代的主流开源大模型大多是 DeepSeek 稀疏注意力（DeepSeek Sparse Attention, DSA） 架构，例如 DeepSeek-V4、Hy4 以及 GLM-5 等1。DSA 架构依赖 Indexer heads 进行动态候选路由，而后主 MLA heads 再在潜空间中进行交互和计算，这意味着，针对传统 Transformer 架构设计的压缩算法无法直接使用，必须针对 DSA 的路由机制，设计一套原生的压缩方案。
因此，我们希望有一种上下文压缩方法，实现如下目的：
在 DSA 架构中，真正参与主注意力计算的 Cache 数量始终保持固定，不随上下文长度的增加而增长。遵循这一结构特性，我们采用基于驱逐式（Eviction-based）的原生压缩：通过语义监督进行探测，并保留被 Indexer heads 命中率较高的 Cache，在后续用户具体的 Query 到达后，再针对问题涉及的局部细节进行按需 Cache 恢复。
在包括 DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 以及 GLM-5.3-Flash 等模型的实验结果表明，提出的上下文压缩方法在 60% 保留率下即可实现无损压缩，任务成功率甚至超过未压缩的全量基线，同时仅引入轻度的额外计算和时间开销。

title: DeepSeek 稀疏注意力架构下的上下文压缩
section: 1 背景：DSA 架构介绍
text:
1 背景：DSA 架构介绍
首先我们先简单回顾一下 DSA 架构，其核心思想是将注意力计算解耦为两个串行部分，首先由轻量级的 索引头（Indexer Heads） 对全量上下文进行相关性打分与 Token 筛选，随后仅在筛选出的 Top-k 位置上，由模型的 多头潜在注意力（Multi-head Latent Attention, MLA） 执行注意力计算并生成后续 Token2。


注 2
事实上，DSA 不一定要和 MLA 绑定，也可以适配 GQA 等架构。但由于上述列出的开源 DSA 大模型都使用 MLA 架构，因此本文默认采用 DSA + MLA 叙述。
给定第 t 个位置的查询隐状态 \mathbf{h}_t \in \mathbb{R}^d，模型需要从与历史上下文位置 s \le t 交互。为了避免注意力遍历全部历史位置带来的高昂开销，首先由一组低维的 Indexer Heads 计算当前位置 t 与历史位置 s 之间的索引得分 I_{t,s}：设共有 H^I 个索引头，第 j 个 Indexer Heads（1 \le j \le H^I）由 \mathbf{h}_t 投影生成低维索引查询向量 \mathbf{q}_{t,j}^{I} \in \mathbb{R}^{d^I} 以及对应的标量权重 w_{t,j}^{I} \in \mathbb{R}。与此同时，每个历史位置 s 在缓存中维护一个跨 Indexer Heads 共享的低维键向量 \mathbf{k}_s^{I} \in \mathbb{R}^{d^I}。而后通过如下公式计算索引得分 I_{t,s}：

I_{t,s} = \sum_{j=1}^{H^I} w_{t,j}^{I} \cdot \operatorname{ReLU}\!\left(\mathbf{q}_{t,j}^{I} \cdot \mathbf{k}_s^{I}\right).

由于 d^I 维度极小且索引键 \mathbf{k}_s^I 跨头共享，该打分过程的计算开销极低。随后根据索引得分 I_{t,s}，从所有历史位置 s \le t 中筛选出得分最高的 Top-k 个位置（一般取 k=2048），构成当前位置 t 的稀疏候选集 \mathcal{C}_t：

\mathcal{C}_t = \operatorname{TopK}_{s \le t}\!\left(I_{t,s},\, k\right).

在确定候选集 \mathcal{C}_t 后，由主注意力层的 H_m 个 MLA Heads 仅该候选集上执行注意力计算并生成后续 Token。MLA 将每个位置 s 的隐状态 \mathbf{h}_s 投影为一个低维的键值潜向量 \mathbf{c}_s^{KV} \in \mathbb{R}^{d_c}（d_c \ll d），并辅以一个携带 ROPE 的共享键分量 \mathbf{k}_s^{R} \in \mathbb{R}^{d_r}：

\mathbf{c}_s^{KV} = W^{DKV} \mathbf{h}_s, \qquad \mathbf{k}_s^{R} = \operatorname{RoPE}\!\left(W^{KR} \mathbf{h}_s\right).

对于被 Indexer Heads 选中的候选位置 s \in \mathcal{C}_t，第 i 个 MLA Head（1 \le i \le H_m）的键向量 \mathbf{k}_{s,i} 与值向量 \mathbf{v}_{s,i} 均由该位置的潜向量 \mathbf{c}_s^{KV} 恢复得到：

\mathbf{k}_{s,i} = \left[W_i^{UK} \mathbf{c}_s^{KV};\, \mathbf{k}_s^{R}\right], \qquad \mathbf{v}_{s,i} = W_i^{UV} \mathbf{c}_s^{KV}.

最终，各 MLA Heads 仅在候选集 \mathcal{C}_t 内部计算主查询向量 \mathbf{q}_{t,i} 与候选键 \mathbf{k}_{s,i} 的注意力权重 \alpha_{t,s}^{(i)}，并加权求和得到当前位置的输出 \mathbf{o}_{t,i}：

\alpha_{t,s}^{(i)} = \frac{\exp\!\left(\mathbf{q}_{t,i}^\top \mathbf{k}_{s,i} / \sqrt{d_k}\right)}{\sum_{s' \in \mathcal{C}_t} \exp\!\left(\mathbf{q}_{t,i}^\top \mathbf{k}_{s',i} / \sqrt{d_k}\right)}, \qquad \mathbf{o}_{t,i} = \sum_{s \in \mathcal{C}_t} \alpha_{t,s}^{(i)} \mathbf{v}_{s,i}.

因此，在 DSA 架构的推理过程中，系统并行维护着两套缓存：用于全局快速路由打分的 Indexer Cache \left\{\mathbf{k}_s^I\right\}，以及用于主注意力计算的 MLA Cache \left\{\left(\mathbf{c}_s^{KV}, \mathbf{k}_s^R\right)\right\}。随着上下文长度 L 的增长，参与 MLA 注意力计算的 Token 数量始终固定为 |\mathcal{C}_t| = k，这将注意力计算复杂度从 O(L^2) 降至 O(Lk)，但这两套物理缓存仍会随上下文的累积而持续线性增长。

title: DeepSeek 稀疏注意力架构下的上下文压缩
section: 2 保留关键 Cache 的上下文压缩
text:
2 保留关键 Cache 的上下文压缩
在探讨具体的压缩算法之前，我们首先明确从原生 Cache 层面做上下文压缩的目标：对于一段历史上下文 H，我们希望构造一段长度更短的 C(H)，使得当后续用户输入 U 到达时，基于压缩生成的输出分布与未压缩时尽可能一致：

p_\theta(y \mid C(H),\, U) \approx p_\theta(y \mid H,\, U).

围绕这一目标3，目前的上下文压缩方法为了减少物理驻留的历史 Cache 数量，大致遵循两种不同的设计理念：


注 3
更准确的说，我们事实上是希望

p_\theta(y \mid C(H),\, U) \approx p_\theta(y \mid R(H,U),\, U).

其中 R(H,U) 表示上下文 H 中真正和用户输入 U 相关的部分。模型在上下文 R(H,U) 下的表现应当高于原始上下文 H 下的表现。

驱逐式压缩（Eviction-based Compression）：从模型注意力的角度出发，剪裁掉那些对后续注意力计算（Q, K, V, O）贡献微小的 Cache，就能在不显著改变输出的前提下，实现上下文压缩。
合并式压缩（Merging-based Compression）：从表征的角度出发，不彻底丢弃信息，而是将键值向量表征按权重融合到保留的代表 Token 上，让合并后的 Cache 贴近原始的全量输出。

那么对于 DSA 架构，哪一种压缩理念更为契合呢？我们回忆一下，在传统的稠密注意力计算中，需要与全部历史位置交互，此时驱逐任何 Cache 都难以避免地造成注意力分布被截断；而对于 DSA 架构，其本身就类似于对稠密注意力做了解耦和剪裁，即使历史上下文累积到了 1M 长度，Indexer 也会在每一层裁掉绝大部分位置，仅保留固定的 k 个进行 MLA 主注意力交互，未被选中的位置对输出的贡献严格为零。
这一结构特性意味着 DSA 其实天然适合驱逐式压缩，既然主注意力本身就只读取少量的 Cache，那么在压缩时，如果能够保留那些在未压缩情况下会被主注意力交互的关键 Cache，那么压缩后的注意力输出在理论上也是完全无损的。
另一方面，从 MLA 的角度来看，其将键打分与值读取信息耦合在同一个共享潜向量 \mathbf{c}_s^{KV} 中。如果采用合并式压缩去改写潜空间表示，不仅容易干扰原有的 Key 路由得分，而且为了适配当前的高效推理后端，可能还需要额外开辟独立的增量页来单独存放 Value 的合并残差。
因此，从 DSA 的稀疏路由本质出发，最适配的方法是驱逐式压缩，这是最契合该架构的压缩切入点。

2.1 结合路由频次与注意力权重的压缩机制
要实现驱逐式的无损压缩，核心是保留那些对生成重要的关键 Cache，而在 DSA 架构下，一个历史 Cache 位置 s 要对模型后续生成产生贡献，必须先被 Indexer Heads 选中进入候选集 \mathcal{C}_t，随后在 MLA Heads 中分配到显著的注意力权重 \alpha_{t,s}。因此，我们的目标是找出那些同时被 Indexer 高频命中，且对 MLA 主注意力贡献显著的历史位置。
为了评估各个历史位置的重要性和注意力贡献，我们构造一组参考查询 R：设历史上下文为 H，用户的输入为 U，我们令参考查询为

R = U \;\|\; P_{\text{study}} \;\|\; T_{\text{chat}} \;\|\; \operatorname{Sample}_n(H).

这里 \| 表示 Cache 序列的拼接，P_{\text{study}} 是固定的学习指令，要求模型总结要点，汇总关键事实，并复述代表性内容，其原文如下：

For cache reconstruction, also do the following: summarize the main points; aggregate all key facts; structure important names, dates, and numerical values as JSON; and repeat representative parts of the documents verbatim.

T_{\text{chat}} 是模型对话模板尾部，\operatorname{Sample}_n(H) 则直接从原始上下文的 Cache ID 中按位置等距抽取若干个 Token，并保持它们的原始顺序。
我们记在历史上下文 H 对应的 Cache 位置集合为 \mathcal{H}， 在 \mathcal{H} 后追加上述参考查询 R，而后通过一次前向传播即可获取 \mathcal{H} 中各 Cache 位置的注意力分布。具体而言，设参考查询 R 的长度为 n ，对第 \ell 层，记第 q 个参考位置（1 \le q \le n）经 Indexer Heads 筛选出的候选集为 \mathcal{C}_{\ell,q}，第 i 个 MLA Head 在该位置上的查询向量为 \tilde{\mathbf{q}}_{\ell,q,i}，候选位置 s \in \mathcal{C}_{\ell,q} 的键向量为 \mathbf{k}_{\ell,s,i}，则模型的主注意力分布 \tilde{\alpha}_{\ell,q,s}^{(i)} 为：

\tilde{\alpha}_{\ell,q,s}^{(i)} = \begin{cases}
\displaystyle\frac{\exp\!\left(\gamma_\ell \tilde{\mathbf{q}}_{\ell,q,i}^\top \mathbf{k}_{\ell,s,i}\right)}{\sum_{u \in \mathcal{C}_{\ell,q}} \exp\!\left(\gamma_\ell \tilde{\mathbf{q}}_{\ell,q,i}^\top \mathbf{k}_{\ell,u,i}\right)}, & s \in \mathcal{C}_{\ell,q}, \\[12pt]
0, & s \notin \mathcal{C}_{\ell,q}.
\end{cases}

其中 \gamma_\ell 为模型原生的注意力缩放系数。由于参考序列 R 包含了对于上下文重点的总结、代表性内容的复述、上下文细节的抽取、以及真实的用户输入消息，因此上述前向过程所激活的候选集序列 \left\{\mathcal{C}_{\ell,q}\right\}_{q=1}^n 与注意力分布 \left\{\tilde{\alpha}_{\ell,q,s}^{(i)}\right\}_{q=1}^n，可以视为真实生成场景下的代理指标，我们也能直接依此量化历史位置 s \in \mathcal{H} 的重要性并挑选出关键 Cache。


2.2 实验设定与结果
模型与推理配置。 实验采用 DeepSeek-V3.2 的 FP8 checkpoint，通过 Transformers 的 8 卡 tensor parallel 运行；全部 61 个 DSA 层参与压缩，主注意力使用原始逻辑位置进行因果屏蔽。推理关闭 thinking，使用 greedy decoding，最多生成 192 token。文档目标保留率分别为 80%、60%、40% 与 20%，完整缓存作为共同基线。
这组实验中，真实问题在压缩前已经明确，参与参考 Q 的构造。正式生成时，指令保持完整，文档使用选中的缓存行，真实问题及模板尾部则拼回完整 prefill 中保存的原始缓存。这构成了本节评测的已知问题压缩流程。
BrowseComp-Plus 的上下文构建。 从 BrowseComp-Plus 的解密问题中，按固定种子的哈希规则选择 100 个不同问题。对每个问题，将官方 gold documents 与 evidence documents 去重后作为正例，再加入官方 hard negatives。正常长度版本以约 10 篇文档为目标，并至少加入 3 篇负例；正例较多时保留全部正例，因此最终每题包含 10 至 16 篇文档，平均 10.7 篇。文档按确定性顺序混排，使用 D01、D02 等编号，末尾附上原始问题。
单篇文档采用约 4096-token 的裁剪预算。正例过长且能找到答案字符串时，围绕答案所在位置保留窗口；其余超长文档保留开头。最终 100 题共包含 1070 个来源文档片段，其中 647 个正例、423 个负例，213 个片段经过裁剪。这些片段拼接后，文档缓存长度为 5,442 至 43,686 token，平均 20,039 token。实验读取这组预先构建好的上下文，并输出证据编号与最终答案。

title: DeepSeek 稀疏注意力架构下的上下文压缩
section: 3 从 V3.2 到 V4：带 Query 的长上下文压缩
text:
3 从 V3.2 到 V4：带 Query 的长上下文压缩
V3.2 采用了首代 DSA 设计，为验证驱逐式压缩提供了一个清晰的起点。不过，V3.2 已是较早的一代模型，其技术报告给出的最大上下文长度为 128K。随着 Agent 持续读取文件、执行工具和积累中间结果，这个窗口很容易被填满；要进一步考察更长历史中的压缩效果，我们需要一个支持更大上下文的模型。
因此，我们将压缩方案迁移到 DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731，把实验范围扩展到 1M 上下文。这一阶段继续沿用第 2 节的任务设定：真实 Query 已经明确，参与参考 Q 的构造，再根据参考前向的访问情况选择并驱逐缓存。

3.1 V4 的注意力架构与压缩适配
V4 的注意力架构将长程记忆分为两种交替使用的路径：

压缩稀疏注意力（Compressed Sparse Attention，CSA）：按 4 个原始 token 的步幅生成一行长期缓存，再由 Indexer 选择相关的压缩行参与主注意力。Flash 模型的原生 Top-k 为 512 行，实现中将这类缓存标记为 C4。
高压缩注意力（Heavily Compressed Attention，HCA）：每 128 个原始 token 生成一行长期缓存，并在这些高度压缩的行上计算稠密注意力，实现中标记为 C128。

两种路径还结合 128-token 滑动窗口，保存近期细节。主注意力使用共享 Key-Value 表示的 MQA。这样，V4 已经在构建长期记忆时减少了缓存行数，我们的驱逐操作进一步在这些原生缓存行中选择保留内容。
将 Token 选择改为原生缓存行选择。 参考后缀仍包含真实 Query、42-token 任务感知学习指令、聊天模板尾部和等距抽取的文档 token。对于每个原生缓存行 j，在参考 Q 上累计其主注意力质量 m_{\ell,j}；对 CSA，再统计 Indexer 路由命中次数 r_{\ell,j}。分别归一化后，CSA 的保留分数为：

g_{\ell,j}^{\mathrm{CSA}}=
\frac{m_{\ell,j}}{\max\!\left(\sum_u m_{\ell,u},\epsilon\right)}
+\frac{r_{\ell,j}}{\max\!\left(\sum_u r_{\ell,u},\epsilon\right)}.

HCA 直接读取其压缩历史，因此使用主注意力质量评分：

g_{\ell,j}^{\mathrm{HCA}}=
\frac{m_{\ell,j}}{\max\!\left(\sum_u m_{\ell,u},\epsilon\right)}.

这里的求和均针对参与选择的文档缓存行，\epsilon=10^{-12}。V4 使用累积注意力质量和路由计数来适配其原生路径；第 2 节 V3.2 中对应的两个分量则是注意力 RMS 与路由频率的平方根。
在统一的原始 Token 预算下处理异构缓存。 文档仍按 B=1024 个原始 token 分配预算；一个完整预算块分别对应 1024/4=256 行 CSA 缓存和 1024/128=8 行 HCA 缓存。各层按自身的评分，在每个块内保留高分行。跨越文档边界的原生行保留，以保护指令等文档外内容。
同一次压缩还需要给调度器提供统一的前缀长度。实现将释放的原始 token 数对齐到 256 的整数倍，再换算成 C4 与 C128 各自的行数。选中行按原始顺序搬入紧凑地址，CSA 的主 Cache 与 Indexer Cache 同步搬移，HCA 则搬移其主缓存。随后更新 vLLM 的请求长度和 block table，并将尾部空闲页面归还缓存池。
保留行继续使用原始位置坐标进行 RoPE 计算，后续 token 按缩短后的物理布局写入。参考后缀的临时状态在正式回答前回退，再在压缩后的缓存上处理真实 Query 并生成答案。


3.2 实验设定与结果
统一的推理设置。 三组实验均采用 DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731，通过 vLLM 进行 TP4 推理，关闭 thinking，使用 greedy decoding，最多生成 192 token。目标文档保留率为 80%、60%、40% 与 20%，参考 Q 预算沿用 n/t=2.5；60% 档仍使用每个 head 1535 个参考 Q。各保留率独立执行带真实 Query 的参考前向，完成缓存筛选后直接回答问题。
从正常长度到百万 Token，再到自然长文档。 我们依次考察三组输入：

BrowseComp-Plus normal100：复用第 2 节 V3.2 的同一批 100 道题及其文档，文档长度为 5,442 至 43,686 token，平均约 20,039 token。这一组用于观察同一压缩思路迁移到 V4 后的表现。
BrowseComp-Plus 1M100：保持上述问题与文档顺序，将文档 token 序列循环拼接，并截取最后一次重复的所需部分，使每题完整输入恰好达到 1,000,000 token。指令与 Query 保持完整，文档部分平均约 999,794 token。这一组将同一批任务扩展到百万 token 的输入规模。
LongBench-v2 473 题：合并前 180 题与后 293 题，使用完整自然文档，不重复或截断。文档长度为 10,137 至 1,045,112 token，平均约 137,731 token，覆盖文档问答、长上下文样本学习、对话、代码和结构化数据等任务。

title: DeepSeek 稀疏注意力架构下的上下文压缩
section: 4 面向未知 Query：通用压缩与信号引导恢复
text:
4 面向未知 Query：通用压缩与信号引导恢复
前两节的压缩都将真实用户消息放进参考后缀，再用它产生的 Q 为历史缓存打分。这样，模型可以围绕当前问题保留证据。不过，Agent 触发 auto compact 时，下一条用户消息往往还没有到来；即使任务没有结束，不同压缩时点之后要处理的子问题也会变化。依据眼前的 Query 压缩，容易提前丢掉下一步才会用到的信息。
因此，我们将流程分成两个阶段：压缩时建立不依赖真实 Query 的通用记忆；问题到来后，再利用模型内部的访问信号定位相关区域，补回当前任务需要的细节。 下面先考察无 Query 压缩造成的变化，再介绍定位 head 的选择，以及压缩与恢复结合后的实验。

4.1 无 Query 压缩：保留通用记忆，也会遗漏局部细节
去掉真实问题，重新构造参考 Q。 无 Query 版本沿用第 3 节的 V4 缓存评分、分块预算与物理压实方法，修改的是参考后缀。设文档为 D，使用一条通用文档学习指令 P_{\mathrm{generic}}，而不拼入真实问题或选项：

R_{\mathrm{generic}}=
P_{\mathrm{generic}}\;\Vert\;T_{\mathrm{chat}}
\;\Vert\;\operatorname{Sample}_{n}(D).

这条指令要求模型建立可供后续任务复用的文档记忆，原文为：

Study the documents above independently of any downstream question. Build a comprehensive, reusable memory of the input. Summarize the central topics, claims, and conclusions; identify the most informative passages; list important entities, relationships, dates, numbers, and exact facts; call out subtle, surprising, exceptional, or easy-to-miss details; note contradictions, uncertainties, and qualifications; and preserve representative wording that may matter for future retrieval. Do not answer any external question.

它在 V4 tokenizer 下为 93 token，与前两节包含真实问题时使用的 42-token 指令不同。目标保留率为 60% 时，仍按 B=1024、n/t=2.5 设置预算：通用指令 93 token、聊天模板尾部 2 token、按文档位置等距抽取的 1535 token，共 1630 token。模型对这段后缀做一次前向，再从中等距选取 1535 个 Q 参与评分。这里的文档抽样直接使用原有 token ID，整个过程不需要自回归生成摘要。
各层由参考访问得到自己的分数 s_\ell，按 1024 个原始 token 的预算块选择保留集合 S_\ell。真实问题随后在压缩后的缓存上重新处理。这样，基础记忆的构建只依赖已读文档，同一套记忆可以等待尚未出现的后续输入。
LongBench-v2 上的变化。 实验沿用第 3 节的 473 道题、完整自然文档，以及 DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731、TP4、关闭 thinking、greedy decoding 和 192-token 生成上限。完整缓存与带 Query 的 60% 压缩都答对 246/473（52.01%）；无 Query 压缩答对 244/473（51.59%），平均实际文档保留率为 60.27%。
总分只少两题，但逐题比较有 37 道原本答对的题变错、35 道原本答错的题变对。分任务结果进一步显示，依赖精细规则和示例映射的任务退化更明显：长上下文样本学习从 51/74 降至 44/74，准确率下降 9.46 个百分点。

案例一：保住操作主题，却混淆快捷键的含义。 一道乐谱软件手册题要求判断移调操作。原文区分了两个动作：普通上下方向键用于半音移调，Ctrl + ↑/↓ 用于八度移调；另一个关键条件是，在移调对话框中不选音符，等同于选中全部音符。完整缓存选对 D，无 Query 压缩后却选了 C，并将 Ctrl + ↑/↓ 解释成半音移调。模型仍记得“音符可以移调”，却没有正确保住区分选项所需的操作细节。
案例二：保住方法名称，却遗漏实现分支。 一道代码题询问 FileManager.write_with_template 的哪项描述有误。关键实现允许 env_callable() 返回字典或字符串：字典进入模板替换，字符串则直接返回。因此，选项 A 中“只使用字典”的说法有误。完整缓存选 A，无 Query 压缩后却选 C，并声称源码中没有 _write_if_changed；实际上，write_with_template 正是通过这个方法写入变更内容。
这两题都指向同一种记忆需求：未来问题可能依赖一条短规则、一个分支，或两个相似操作之间的差别。 通用参考能保留文档的主要访问模式，但这些局部信息未必得到足够高的分数。后面的恢复记录也保存了对应区域在基础选择中的缺失行，可以继续检查定位信号能否将它们找回。


4.2 定位 Head：从模型的读取行为找到相关区域
为什么可以从内部信号定位？ 问题进入模型后，各层 Q 会随着问题内容和前层读取结果变化。某个 head 的输出可以写为：

o_{h,q}=\sum_j\alpha_{h,q,j}v_j.

这里的 \alpha_{h,q,j} 记录这个 head 在处理问题位置 q 时，如何分配对历史缓存的读取。我们的出发点是：某些 head 的访问会集中到与问题有关的段落，可以把这种读取行为当作模型内部的定位信号。不同 head 的访问模式不同，直接平均全部 head 容易稀释局部峰值，因此需要找出证据定位能力较强的一小组 head。
压缩后的缓存不一定已经足以回答问题，但相关段落中的部分行可能仍然保留着实体、主题或上下文特征。问题激活这些存活行时，它们的原始位置坐标就能指向值得重新读取的区域。我们据此恢复整个局部窗口，补齐同一区域中此前被驱逐的行。定位使用的是压缩记忆留下的线索，内容则由保存的原始缓存提供。
扫描并固定定位 head。 定位实验包含 156 道题：68 道 LongBench-v2 与 88 道接近 128K 上下文的 BrowseComp-Plus。先固定每题无 Query、60% 保留率的基础选择，再在 41 个参与压缩的层上采集完整问题的主注意力与 Indexer 信号，对照离线标注的证据区域，比较 head、窗口大小和组合方式。最终用于 V4 恢复的是四个主注意力 head：

\mathcal H=\{
\texttt{L20-H5},\ \texttt{L20-H30},\
\texttt{L20-H31},\ \texttt{L26-H58}\}.

层号与全局 head 号均从 0 开始。这组 head 由 LongBench 的定位排名选出，随后固定用于完整 LongBench-v2 与 InfiniteBench 实验4。


注 4
发现集中的 68 道 LongBench-v2 题来自后文同一批 473 题，包含早期压缩退化案例。InfiniteBench 直接复用选定的 head 与恢复预算，没有重新选 head。证据标注用于离线排名和定位评估；逐题恢复只使用问题与模型信号。
把问题的读取转成窗口分数。 将原始位置划分为 128-token 窗口。对 head h 所在层 \ell(h)、问题后缀位置 q 和窗口 w，累加该窗口中存活行的注意力概率：

a_{h,q,w}=\sum_{j\in S_{\ell(h)}\cap w}\alpha_{h,q,j}.

这些概率使用 V4 原生注意力的归一化，分母包含实际路由到的 CSA 行、因果滑动窗口与 attention sink。probe 只访问基础选择 S_\ell；未保留的文档行不参与这次读取。实现还将重构的注意力输出与原生 kernel 对照，核验归一化是否一致。
对每个窗口，在完整问题后缀的各位置中取最大的 5 个注意力质量，再求均值；问题位置不足 5 个时全部使用：

u_{h,w}=\operatorname{MeanTop5}_{q}(a_{h,q,w}).

这样，问题中的关键实体或操作词即使只在少数位置强烈访问证据，也能留下清楚的窗口信号。随后，对各 head 在可见窗口上的分数做 Z 标准化，消除不同 head 的数值尺度差异，再等权平均：

z_{h,w}=\frac{u_{h,w}-\mu_h}{\max(\sigma_h,10^{-6})},
\qquad
g_w=\frac{1}{|\mathcal H|}\sum_{h\in\mathcal H}z_{h,w}.

其中 \mu_h、\sigma_h 是该 head 在可见窗口上的均值和标准差。对某个 head 不可见的窗口，其合并贡献置零；所有 head 都不可见的窗口不进入候选。最后选取分数最高的 24 个窗口，得到最多覆盖 3072 个原始 token 的恢复区域 R。

4.3 无 Query 压缩加恢复：方法与两组基准结果

title: DeepSeek 稀疏注意力架构下的上下文压缩
section: 6 跨模型泛化：GLM-5.3 与 DeepSeek-V4.1
text:
6 跨模型泛化：GLM-5.3 与 DeepSeek-V4.1
前面的实验主要围绕 DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 展开。接下来，我们将“通用参考构造 → 缓存筛选 → 真实 Query 探测 → 局部恢复”迁移到两种不同的架构：GLM-5.3-Flash 在稀疏注意力之外引入了线性注意力状态，DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 则进一步让多个层共享 KV 与路由信息。这里考察的是，同一套筛选与恢复思路能否适配这些变化，并保持模型原有的任务表现。
两组实验均采用 60% 基础保留率与 24 × 128 token 的净增加恢复预算。通用 reference 不包含真实问题；问题到达后，probe 只读取已冻结的基础选择。定位 head 在各模型上重新扫描和选择，随后固定用于后续评测。各模型使用自己的 tokenizer、聊天模板与原生缓存格式，结果分别与本模型的完整缓存基线比较。

6.1 GLM-5.3-Flash：线性与稀疏注意力的混合架构
架构与压缩适配。 GLM-5.3-Flash 采用线性注意力与稀疏注意力交替的混合架构。按模型配置，其文本主干共 45 层，包括 34 层 Kimi Delta Attention（KDA）和 11 层 DSA，大体按三层 KDA、一层 DSA 的顺序排列，最后再接一层 KDA。KDA 将历史信息累积到固定大小的递归状态中；DSA 层则保留可按位置寻址的历史缓存，供 Indexer 和主注意力读取。
我们据此将驱逐式压缩作用于 11 个 DSA 层。GLM 的 Indexer 将每 4 个原始 token 组成一个池化单元，筛选时将主注意力质量与路由次数汇总到这些单元，再在每个 1024-token 文档块内分配保留配额。保留或恢复一个单元时，同时处理对应的四个主缓存位置与 Indexer 行，使两条缓存流保持一致。
KDA 状态与池化尾部状态完整保留。 Reference 和 query probe 都是临时前向，结束后需要回退它们对这些状态的修改，再用最终记忆正式回答。恢复窗口仍以原始 token 坐标定位；补入缺失单元后，将选中的缓存按原顺序物理压实，更新调度页表并归还尾部页面。因此，这组实验包含实际的物理缓存释放。
Reference 使用与 V4 相同的通用学习指令和文档均匀采样规则。经 GLM 原生 tokenizer 编码，后缀总长为 1632 token，从中均匀选取 1535 个 Q 参与评分。推理采用 TP4、FP8 主缓存与 Indexer Cache、greedy decoding，并使用空的闭合 think 块作为生成起始模板。
重新定位 Head。 我们沿用第 4 节的 156 题发现队列，用 GLM 的 tokenizer 重新映射证据位置，在 11 个 DSA 层上扫描主注意力 head。先冻结无 Query 的基础选择，再让完整问题读取这段记忆；根据离线证据定位排名，选出四个 head：

\mathcal H_{\mathrm{GLM}}=\{
\texttt{L27-H47},\ \texttt{L27-H58},\
\texttt{L39-H43},\ \texttt{L35-H26}\}.

层号与全局 head 号均从 0 开始。恢复时，对每个 head 的 128-token 窗口注意力质量取完整问题上的 Top-5 均值，再做跨窗口 Z 标准化和四头等权平均，选取最高的 24 个窗口。注意力重构结果与原生 kernel 输出做过核对。具有可用标注的样本共 152 题，其中主要定位评估结果为：

6.2 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash：跨层共享 KV 的稀疏架构
架构与压缩适配。 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 采用因果编码器—解码器（Causal Encoder-Decoder，CED）结构：40 层文本主干分为 20 层因果编码器与 20 层解码器，解码器的全局 KV 由编码器末层隐状态投影得到。它使用的 Compressed Sparse Attention 2（CSA2）通过 Full、Reindex 和 Reuse 三种模式跨层共享主 KV、Indexer 键与候选索引，解码器中的分层 Indexer 还会复用前层建立的候选池。
这使得缓存的物理存储和使用它的注意力层之间存在多对一关系：不同层可以读取同一份 KV，却对哪些历史位置重要给出不同判断。若直接按某一层的选择搬移共享缓存，其他层的路由与位置映射也会受到影响。
我们因此为 38 个使用全局稀疏缓存的层（L2–L39）分别维护逻辑选择集合，在每个使用层自己的 Indexer logits 上应用掩码，随后再执行原生 Top-k。即使该层复用了前层的索引器，也根据当前层的选择重新路由，并保留共享源提供给后续层的候选信息。编码器中每行对应 2 个原始 token、解码器中每行对应 1 个原始 token 的缓存，统一换算到原始坐标后分配筛选预算和恢复窗口。
Reference 与 probe 结束后，原生滑动窗口、压缩器状态及 Engram 的短历史哈希状态均回退到文档读完时的状态；Engram 参数表和原始位置坐标保留。真实问题选出窗口后，将对应行加入各层的逻辑可见集合，再重新处理问题并生成答案。
当前 V4.1 实验保留共享物理缓存，通过逻辑掩码限制各层可见内容。 它检验的是筛选与恢复后的任务质量，完整物理前缀一直保留到 decode 结束；跨层共享缓存的物理压实与页面释放仍需进一步实现。

7.1 边读边压，保留追加空间

这组记录每题触发 1 至 9 次压缩。每个原始文档 token 只做一次文档前向；后面的 token 读取的是前面各轮形成的记忆，因此这组缓存与一次性完整长前向产生的缓存也不完全相同。


7.2 用 CPU 归档提供最后的恢复来源
中间各轮产生的原生缓存行按原始坐标归档到 CPU。真实 query 只在文档读完后进入 probe，读取当前 GPU 上的物理记忆；选出 24 个窗口后，再从 CPU 归档中补入对应缺失行。
因此，这个系统限制的是 GPU 上的活动缓存容量，CPU 归档仍随已读历史增长。它探索了分层记忆中的一种取舍：较小的活动记忆配合较大的可恢复历史。

title: 从模型的随机数指纹出发：一项关于 LLM 推理回路的研究
text:
一直以来，围绕如何判断 GPT「降智」或者说路由到小模型的讨论层出不穷。一篇 LINUX DO 帖子 提出了一种简单的判断方法：让模型从给定范围中随机选择数字，多次采样它的输出分布，并将其当作统计指纹来识别模型1。
这个方法为何能区分不同模型并不难理解，但相比之下，另一个问题似乎更有值得研究：
为了研究该问题，我们从提示词「在 1–300 中随机选择一个数」出发，定位到了一类会强烈读取候选范围 300 的 heads（Sec 2）。进一步的实验逐渐揭示出其更一般的作用：读取推理任务的候选集合，当答案尚未被有效推理出来、模型仍需在多个候选之间进行竞争时，这些 heads 写入残差流的信息会显著改变输出（Sec 3）。
而当我们在正常的推理过程中，手动截断模型的推理回路（例如删除关键推理链，或者屏蔽 retrieval heads），使模型陷入不确定性推理时，这类 heads 的因果效应同样会被显著放大（Sec 4）。这似乎揭示模型中存在两种相互竞争的回路：当模型能正常推理时，推理回路生效，而这类 heads 对应的回路被抑制；当推理回路被切断后，这种回路则产生因果效应，开始主导模型的行为。
基于此，我们将这类 heads 的表现作为模型推理是否可信的信号，并且在检测到不可信推理时，启动推理增强策略，结果表明其的确能检测到不可信推理并增强模型的性能（Sec 5）。额外的实验表明，这类 heads 同样存在于线性注意力和稀疏注意力架构的模型中（Sec 6）。

title: 从模型的随机数指纹出发：一项关于 LLM 推理回路的研究
section: 1 背景：LLM 的非随机输出
text:
1 背景：LLM 的非随机输出
当我们向大语言模型输入下面这段提示词时：

请从 1–300 随机选择一个数，只输出这个数字。

模型并不会在前向传播中真正「抽取」一个随机数。更准确地说，语言模型的前向传播是一个从输入文本到生成 token logits 的确定性函数。随后，解码器根据温度 T 将 logits 转换为概率分布：

p_i = \frac{\exp(z_i/T)}{\sum_j \exp(z_j/T)}.

因此，在输入 prompt 和解码设置均固定的情况下，模型为下一个 token 给出的概率分布 p 也是固定的2。
在采样解码中，采样器会使用伪随机数从分布 p 中选取 token。因此，模型的单次输出可能变化，长期统计分布却应当保持稳定。这解释了随机数选择为什么能够形成模型指纹：不同模型具有不同的架构和参数，会为各个数字 token 分配不同的生成概率，重复采样后，概率则表现为可识别的输出分布。


注 2
实际推理服务未必能做到逐 bit 可复现。vLLM、SGLang 等推理后端中的批处理和并行归约可能改变浮点运算顺序，从而产生数值差异。可参见 Thinking Machines Lab 的博客：Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference。
我们真正关注的问题是：这种概率分布在模型前向传播过程中，是如何被写入和生成的？

title: 从模型的随机数指纹出发：一项关于 LLM 推理回路的研究
section: 2 写入随机数指纹的 Head
text:
2 写入随机数指纹的 Head
在 LLM 前向传播的过程中，QK 决定了注意力从哪里读取，OV 决定了向残差流写入什么，这些信息在 MoE 中被读取和处理，最终在输出层形成 logits 分布。
对于随机数生成任务，按照上述对 LLM 信息流的理解，一个合理的推测是：模型的深层可能存在一些 heads，它们编码了 1–300 这一范围信息，让下游计算可以读取随机数的选取区间。该信息被写入残差流并形成输出，模型的选择偏好也在这一过程中被写入。
从这一推测出发，我们在 MOE 模型 Qwen3-235B-A22B 上进行实验。我们构造与「请从1-300随机选择一个数，只输出这个数字」类似的多条中文 prompts，其均要求模型从 1–300 中随机选择一个数，但采用了不同的语义表述。
实验结果表明，不同 prompts 的具体概率分布会有所变化，但整体结构保持稳定：生成 token 的概率质量几乎全部集中在数字上，且数字 1 和 2 始终构成最主要的竞争3。


注 3
我倾向于认为，1 和 2 的概率高于其他数字，是由预训练语料中的数字分布决定的；但是，模型对数字 1、2 之间的明显偏好，更像是在后训练中被编码的。

2.1 Head 定位
Qwen3-235B-A22B 共有 94 层、每层 64 个 query heads。我们对每个 head 进行消融观察，在该层 attention 的 o_proj 之前，将目标 head 在所有输入 token 位置的 128 维输出切片置零，同时保持其他计算不变。
为了衡量消融前后完整词表概率分布的差异，我们使用总变差距离（total variation distance，TV）：


\operatorname{TV}(h,l)
=\operatorname{TV}\!\left(p,p^{(h,l)}\right)
=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{v\in\mathcal V}
\left|p(v)-p^{(h,l)}(v)\right|.


其中 p 是原始下一 token 分布，p^{(h,l)} 是删除 head (h,l) 后的分布。TV 越大，说明这个 head 对当前输出分布的因果影响越强。
通过实验，我们定位到最显著的 head 为 L82.H18，其全词表 TV 达到 34.0%，在所有 heads 中最强4。


注 4
L82.H18 在中心化全词表 logit \operatorname{RMS}_{c}(h,l) 中同样排名第一，其定义为：

\operatorname{RMS}_{c}(h,l)=
\sqrt{\frac{1}{|\mathcal V|}\sum_{v\in\mathcal V}
\left(\Delta z_v^{(h,l)}-\overline{\Delta z}^{(h,l)}\right)^2}.

其中 \Delta z_v^{(h,l)} 为删除 head (h,l) 后 token v 的 logit 变化，\overline{\Delta z}^{(h,l)} 为其全词表均值。\operatorname{RMS}_{c}(h,l) 表示删除该 head 对全词表 logit 结构的整体影响。





图 1(a)：L82.H18 周围的局部 TV 热图。







图 1(b)：删除 L82.H18 后 P(1) 和 P(2) 变化。




删除 L82.H18 后，所有 prompts 的 P(1) 均下降，平均变化为 −33.80 个百分点；与此同时，P(2) 平均变化为 +33.54 个百分点，其余输出概率几乎不变。
这说明，我们定位出的 L82.H18 的确在数字候选内部写入了强烈偏好。


2.2 Head 注意力分布
我们进一步观察 L82.H18 的注意力分布，所使用的 prompts 均包含 28 个 tokens，且具有相似的结构，其中 300 被拆为 t7–t9 三个 tokens，模型侧的 assistant 位于 t22，正式回答前的最后一个 \n\n 位于 t27。




图 2：经 chat template 渲染后的 28-token 随机数选择 prompt。



实验结果表明，L82.H18 最集中的注意力连接是从 token \n\n（t27）到 token 300（t7–t9），注意力质量平均为 99.56%，下图展示了其中 5 条代表性 prompts 的注意力分布。




图 3：L82.H18@q27 在 5 条代表性 prompts 上的注意力分布。每行表示一条 prompt，每列表示一个 token 位置，token 300 始终在 t7–t9 位置。



换言之，在模型开始准备生成答案时，L82.H18 几乎只从范围边界 300 读取信息，再把得到的向量写入到回答开始位置。


2.3 Head 注意力干预
为了判断上述显著注意力边是否真正主导输出变化，我们在相同的 prompts 上，进一步进行如下几种对 L82.H18 的注意力干预实验：


完整模型：不进行任何干预，作为基线。
删除 L82.H18：将 L82.H18 在所有 token 位置的输出置零。
删除 \n\n → 300 注意力边：只将 q27 指向 t7–t9 的三条边置零。
删除 L82.H18 后补回 \n\n → 300 写入：先删除 L82.H18，再在 t27 补入主要由 t7–t9 贡献的原始残差写入向量，其余 token 位置仍保持删除。


前三种实验检验 \n\n → 300 注意力边是否主导 L82.H18 的行为；第四种实验补回这条边写入残差流的信息，检验能否恢复完整 head 的作用。




图 4：四种条件（完整模型、删除 L82.H18、删除 \n\n → 300 注意力边、删除 L82.H18 后补回 \n\n → 300 写入）下生成 token 1 的概率、生成 token 2 的概率和全词表 TV。



实验结果表明，删除 \n\n → 300 注意力边后，其效应能达到删除完整 L82.H18 效应的 96.95%。在删除完整 L82.H18 后，仅补回 \n\n → 300 主导的残差写入，能恢复原始删除效应的 97.33%。
这说明 L82.H18 的主要作用的确是候选范围信息搬运到回答位置，并促进在输出中形成模型指纹。

title: 从模型的随机数指纹出发：一项关于 LLM 推理回路的研究

3 Head 泛化实验
目前为止，我们证明了 L82.H18 在「从 1–300 中随机选数」这一任务中的特性。接下来一个自然的问题是：这种特性的泛化性如何，L82.H18 能在其它任务中展现出类似的「将候选信息汇总搬运，并促进形成模型指纹」这一特性么，以及它是否能够具有更一般的功能？
为此，我们进行了泛化实验，改变候选类型与约束、下游任务与推理长度，以探究 head 在各种场景下的功能。

3.1 候选类型泛化实验
我们先检验最直接的泛化：如果把数字候选换成其他类型的候选，L82.H18 是否仍会展现出相同的特性？为此，我们将原任务中的 1–300 替换成字母范围：

请从 A 到 D 中任选一个，只输出这个字母。

实验结果与数字范围几乎一致，L82.H18 对字母 D 的注意力高达 88.62%，删除这条显著注意力边后，TV 达到 30.3%。
我们进一步把输入候选扩展为显式列表，以检验该特性能否扩展到一般候选集合。所有实验都使用如下相同模板：

请从候选列表【……】中任选一个，只输出被选中的候选。

规范列表：列表内元素本身具有强烈的顺序关系，并且按照该顺序排列，例如天干列表【甲、乙、丙、丁……】。
非规范列表：列表元素之间不存在稳定的内在顺序，排列顺序杂乱，例如食物列表【饺子、面条、米饭、包子……】。

3.2 候选约束泛化实验

3.3 任务类型泛化实验
我们接下来探究 L82.H18 的特性是否能泛化到更多的任务上，而不仅局限于随机选择。我们保持输入范围 1–300，构建多种下游任务，初步的观察表明，head 的因果影响性似乎与任务允许的答案个数有关。具体来说，我们根据任务类型将其分为两组：

非唯一性任务：任务的答案具备非唯一性，有多个合法答案，模型输出其中任何一个即满足任务要求。
唯一性任务：任务的答案具备唯一性，仅有一个合法答案，模型仅输出该答案才满足任务要求。

因此，L82.H18 不能被视为只在随机选择任务中才生效的 head。它在更多的任务中仍会注意到候选范围，这意味着其会把范围信息运送到回答位置；但是似乎只有当答案尚未被确定、模型仍需要在多个候选之间分配概率时，下游任务才会使用这份信息。

3.5 候选信息搬运 Head 泛化实验
在之前的实验中，我们以 L82.H18 为研究对象，但正如 Sec 3.1 中所指出的，这组 heads 只有在列表内部具备明显的序关系时，才会展现出较强的因果效应。
那么，对于序关系不那么强的列表，是否也存在一族 heads 具备类似的功能？事实上，从 Transformer circuit 的角度来看，类似的 heads 是应当存在的8。基于此，我们进行实验，观察一般列表下是否有类似功能的 heads。


注 8
因为模型负责某个功能的回路被分散了，最终落在多个层和不同的 head 中，导致一族 heads 可能会负责相似的功能，但是具体的生效或者激活场景有所差异。
类似 Sec 2 的设定，我们构建了多个随机的无序候选列表，并分别执行随机选择和确定性选择任务，而后扫描模型全部 heads，在 attention 的 o_proj 之前将输出切片置零。我们将筛选分数定义为


S(h,l)=\max\!\left(\Delta \operatorname{TV}(h,l),0\right)\times A(h,l),


其中 \Delta \operatorname{TV}(h,l) 是随机选择与确定性选择之间，删除 head 后的 \operatorname{TV} 之差；A(h,l) 是随机选择下 head 对候选列表的总注意力。该指标要求定位的 heads 显著读取候选列表，且其因果效应主要出现在答案尚未确定时，这样做是为了排除语法 heads 或 ICL heads 等干扰。
所有 heads 的 S(h,l) 指标热力图如下所示，我们选取得分最高的 6 个 heads（L80.H42、L82.H21、L85.H49、L89.H53、L87.H14、L88.H13 ）作为代表性 heads。




图 8：全模型 heads 的 S(h,l) 指标热图，我们挑选出的得分最高的 6 个 heads 已经标出。



更多的实验表明，这些 heads 与 L82.H18 展现出相似作用：答案未决时，它们读取候选列表，删除后会明显改变输出分布；答案已经确定时，其因果效应则接近消失。为了保持博客的可读性，我们不再赘述这些实验，在 Sec 4 中，我们会使用上述的更一般性的 heads 进行实验，进一步揭示其工作机制和信息回路。

title: 从模型的随机数指纹出发：一项关于 LLM 推理回路的研究
section: 4 推理回路截断下 Head 的因果效应
text:
4 推理回路截断下 Head 的因果效应
经过 Sec 3 的实验，我们定位出了一族 heads，其具备以下功能：

当答案未被有效推理出来、模型仍需在多个候选之间进行竞争时，下游任务会强烈使用这族 heads 搬运的候选信息

这一功能可以泛化到不同的候选类型、不同的候选约束、不同的任务类型，以及包含长程思考的回答过程。
我们进一步从 Transformer circuit 的角度审视这一结果，相关研究表明，模型的前向传播输出并不是由单一信号决定的，不同回路会将多种信号写入残差流，并最终共同决定输出。其中有一个重要的洞见是：

通常在多个回路的竞争中，最强的信号会主导模型行为，其他信号虽然仍然存在，但会在输出时被压制；但是当原本主导的回路变弱甚至截断时，次强回路便获得更大的相对权重，并对缺失的信息进行的补偿，并取代主导地位。在规模更大、信息表示更加分散的模型中，这种回路之间的竞争机制尤其明显。

从这个角度来看，先前定位出的 heads 共同参与了一类回路：当模型能够正常推理时，确定性推理的信号占据主导，这类回路的写入难以影响最终输出，删除后产生的 TV 很小；当正常推理信号较弱，或者相应回路被截断时，这类回路便会获得更大的因果效应，删除后的 TV 显著上升。
Sec 3.3 和 Sec 3.4 的实验已经初步支持了这一观点。我们进一步采用主动的干预实验进行检验，通过多种方法破坏模型正常推理的回路，而后观察候选 heads 的因果效应是否会如预期般增强。

4.1 回路起始截断：删除输入证据
为了破坏模型的推理回路，最直接的方法是在输入时删除关键证据，这可以被视为破坏推理回路的起始点。
为此，我们选取 DROP、BrowseComp-Plus、2WikiMultiHopQA 和 MuSiQue 这四个数据集，构造反事实的问答样例：每个问题都被改写，正确答案及其他候选均被替换为随机生成的临时代号，代号的拼写和数字不包含任何可供推断的规律，以防止模型利用参数化记忆回答问题。
每个样例都如下包含完整证据和缺乏证据的版本：

完整证据：保留输入中所有的证据，模型能够正常推理。
缺乏证据：删除输入中推理所需要的关键证据，使模型无法推理出正确答案。

我们在回答开始的位置，联合删除 Sec 3.5 中挑选出 heads 的写入，而后计算全词表分布的 TV。

4.2 回路中段截断：删除关键推理链
接下来我们删除模型 thinking 中能够推理出答案的关键链路，并观察 heads 的因果效应变化，这可以被视为破坏推理回路的中段。

4.3 回路末端截断：删除 Retrieval Head
之前我们分别从截断了推理回路的起始和中段，现在我们考虑截断其末端：保持问题和输入证据完整，只屏蔽负责从上下文中搬运答案的 retrieval heads9。此时虽然答案证据仍然存在，但是模型失去了利用其的能力。

section: 5 基于 Head TV 检测的增强推理
text:
5 基于 Head TV 检测的增强推理
通过先前的实验，我们已经了解搬运候选信息 heads 的功能：当答案尚未被有效推理出来时，其对输出分布的影响效应会显著增强。那么，能否利用这一机制增强模型的推理性能？具体来说，我们能否采用如下性能增强方式：

在正常推理输出答案后，检测候选 heads 的 TV 值，若 TV 超过阈值，投入额外的开销加强推理。

我们还是在 DROP、BrowseComp-Plus、2WikiMultiHopQA 和 MuSiQue 数据集上进行实验，构造 Agent 式工作流，让模型基于检索到的信息进行推理。在推理结束并输出答案后，我们在最后一轮输出正式开始的位置，删除 heads 的写入并计算全词表 TV10。


注 10
由于只需要在正式回答前的最后一个 \n\n 位置进行干预，因此之前所有 tokens 均可以 prefix cache 复用，这保证了 TV 检测的低开销。具体实现中，我们通过 vLLM 的 llm.collective_rpc() 在各个 worker 上调用 set_rag_tv_probe()，切换候选 heads 的消融状态。
根据 Sec 4 的实验结果，我们经验性地将 TV 阈值固定为 6%。当 TV 超过该阈值时，Agent 工作流将继续执行，将更多检索的信息输入给模型，并追加新的用户 prompt，提示模型之前的输出可能缺乏证据，要求模型继续推理并确定答案。




图 9：基于 TV 检测的推理增强结果，图片展示了每个数据集上的原始推理成功率、TV 超过阈值的频率、推理增强后的成功率。



可以看到，四个数据集上 TV 检测均能识别未被有效推理的轨迹，且在增强推理后能带来的成功率收益。这说明 TV 检测的确可以作为一种不可信推理的代理指标，并且提供一定程度的修复。
需要说明的是，方法只能检测出模型内部未能形成稳定推理回路的不可信推理；对于模型认为可信、但实际上错误的推理，无法被 TV 检测出来。

尽管如此，但是实验表明类似轨迹 B 的推理，其 TV 仍然显著高于那些可信且正确的推理。这说明一些不可信或者不确定的信号虽然没有出现在模型自然语言的输出中，但是还是引起了表征空间的改变，从而能被 TV 检测到。
因此，搬运候选信息 heads 的 TV 值可以视为不可信推理的代理指标。当然，这种不可信的信号也可能会反映在模型的推理链中，但相比之下，TV 值能够检测到一些不会在自然语言中表达出来的信号（如 注 11 所述）。此外，一些指标如生成 Token 时的分布熵，也能捕获一些相关信号，但这类 Token 级别的指标都是局部代理，无法像 TV 值一样识别出整个推理过程的不确定性。

title: 从模型的随机数指纹出发：一项关于 LLM 推理回路的研究
section: 7 总结与思考
text:
7 总结与思考
本文从随机数选择任务中稳定出现的模型指纹出发，定位出了一类搬运候选信息的 heads。我们发现，当答案未被有效推理出来、模型仍需在多个候选之间进行竞争时，这类 heads 会产生显著的因果效应。其作用不仅能够跨候选、跨任务、跨架构泛化，也在多种截断正常推理回路的干预实验中稳定复现。我们进一步将这类 heads 的 TV 值作为不可信推理的检测信号，并用它触发额外推理增强，从而提升模型的推理性能。
当然，需要承认的是，博客并没有将模型的指纹是如何产生的这一问题研究清楚。尽管我最开始是希望分析一下随机数指纹是如何形成的，但是随后我意识到，很难在不看训练数据或者训练动态的情况下研究这件事情。并且，后训练时仅需要少量的轨迹，就可以大幅改变模型的偏好，这也使得分析较为困难。意识到这一点后，我改变了思路，开始观察模型的信息流，并逐渐得出了目前博客的结果。
在所有实验现象中，最值得思考的就是模型中信息回路之间的竞争：为什么推理回路被截断后，对搬运候选信息 heads 消融产生的 TV 值就会变大？一个直接的观点是：这类 heads 的信号强度是不变的，但是推理回路被截断后，模型的困惑度变高，导致 logit 和概率分布变均匀了，因此固定的信号强度带来的影响随之增大。
这种看法不能说是错的，但是只从 logit 或者 softmax 的角度来看，太偏向事后分析了，无法解释很多现象。本身 logit 就不具备一致的变化倾向，heads 对于 logit 的影响也不是一致的；在 Sec 5 的实验中，也出现了多处模型在不可信推理的回答时，输出概率分布极度尖锐，但还是具有相当大的 TV 值的现象；此外，我们也无法解释为什么只有定位出来的 heads 对输出分布有较大影响，其对 logit 的绝对值影响是不大的，有时候甚至很轻微。从消融实验的结果来看，heads 写入了更多信息、网络对相同的写入产生了更大的传播、最终的 softmax 变得更敏感似乎会同时发生，相互耦合。
尽管如此，目前的一些发现倒也足以提高推理性能了。理解模型或者说做可解释性的目的也在于此，需要解决具体的问题或者足够实用，不能单纯为了解释而解释，尤其是必须考虑泛化性层次的一些东西。一些工作比如 J-Space，也是从模型理解出发，最终提出方案约束模型行为。当然，如何能够在目前的框架下，更好的理解模型，那就是后续需要继续探究的事情了。
